art_deco-fete-v2.skip_reason: Tool limitation: the small letterspaced Deco list is split into word fragments; at 16px the letter gaps are too pixel-coarse to pass the tracking evenness test.

art_deco-gig-v2.skip_reason: The gold type and the gold Deco ornament are the same colour and much the same scale, so nothing measurable separates them. On a pure black ground the neutral masks are empty and everything lands in one colour mask of 400,000 pixels: rays, borders and lettering alike. That yields 19 candidate lines of which only about 8 are text, and the aligner puts the headline on a 21-pixel band. The type is font-like and the ground is flat, so this is a limit of telling ornament from lettering, not of the poster.

art_nouveau-fete-v2.skip_reason: The title is drawn, not set. Art Nouveau lettering of this kind is built to its own line: the letters of 'Brindlewick Village Fete' vary in width and slope to fill the arc, the terminals grow into the surrounding foliage, and the whole is part of the ornamental frame rather than a typeface applied to it. No face can stand in for it. The frame itself is continuous with the lettering, so the artwork cannot be cut out from behind the words either. Measured, the solver rejects 63 bands against the 22 it keeps and cannot align the copy better than a mean cost of 1.11.

art_nouveau-gig-v2.skip_reason: Custom Art Nouveau headline lettering integrated into the curves of the illustration.

atelier_populaire-fete-v2.skip_reason: Hand-lettered, screen-printed slogan integrated with the image.

atelier_populaire-gig-v2.skip_reason: The headline is brush-drawn, not set. Every letter is an individual stroke: the two R's of CARVER differ in width, angle and terminal, the A is asymmetric, and the edges are ragged where the brush ran dry, so no typeface can stand in for it without replacing the poster's whole character. The silkscreened fist is drawn by the same hand and overlaps the lettering (the ticket crosses the R), so the artwork cannot be cut out from behind the type either. Measured, the solver finds only 4 text bands where the copy needs 8, because the strokes merge into each other and into the illustration. This is a limit of resetting drawn lettering as type, not of the poster.

belle_epoque_lithograph-fete-v2.skip_reason: The lettering is hand-drawn lithographic display type woven into the illustration, on shifting baselines.

belle_epoque_lithograph-gig-v2.skip_reason: The display lettering is hand-drawn lithography. 'CARVER & THE FLOOD' carries a drawn outline and a cast shadow that are part of each letter rather than an effect applied to a face, the strokes swell and taper by hand, and the words are fitted around the dancer rather than set on a line. Resetting them in a typeface would remove the thing the style consists of. Measured, 71 bands are rejected against 25 kept, and the copy cannot be aligned better than a mean cost of 1.07.
